incidents.victim: FBI, Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing), and 40+ Organizations via Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day
incidents.vector: Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft SaaS zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) and bypassed WAF rules via URL-encoding to breach federal, aviation, healthcare, and technology organizations.
incidents.impact: ~5,000 FBI personnel records stolen including medical, psychiatric, and clandestine unit data; Jeppesen ForeFlight (Boeing aviation nav subsidiary, $10.55B acquisition) extorted with safety-sensitive flight data; three gang members arrested in Jordan, Netherlands, and Canada.

incidents.victim: US Government, Critical Manufacturing, Healthcare, IT Sector, and Allies (Japan, Poland, Taiwan, Africa)
incidents.attacker: China — state-sponsored espionage group (Integrity Technology Group)
incidents.vector: Chinese government-linked company Integrity Technology Group enabled threat actors using automated scanning (Microscan), large-scale botnets, living-off-the-land techniques, and commercial VPN infrastructure to gain persistent access across critical sectors.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data exfiltrated from US critical infrastructure including power utilities, government agencies, and hospitals; DOJ/FBI seized two hacking tools (Microscan, FishHub) on October 8; joint advisory issued by CISA, NSA, FBI, and allied intelligence agencies.

incidents.victim: Corporate Travelers at Global Hotels
incidents.vector: Russian FSB subgroup manipulated DNS and HTTP traffic at hotel networks to redirect business travelers to device-code phishing pages and fake Microsoft login portals, harvesting credentials, session tokens, and device security configurations.
incidents.impact: Cloud identity compromise and persistent endpoint malware installed on targeted traveler devices; ongoing campaign spanning multiple countries, primarily targeting government and business personnel in transit.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian Transportation, Manufacturing, and Energy Organizations
incidents.vector: Spear-phishing emails with archive attachments deliver evolving VBScript payloads that install the MatchBoil downloader, which executes every two minutes to retrieve updated MatchWok backdoor components from attacker infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Persistent covert access established across Ukraine's critical industrial sectors; MatchBoil malware continuously updates its payload to evade detection; assessed as a probable precursor to destructive operations against Ukrainian infrastructure.

incidents.victim: Taiwan Research and Policy Organizations
incidents.vector: AI-assisted spear-phishing using real academic conference themes and impersonation of policy institutions, delivering real-time Google adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) phishing pages to harvest credentials from targeted individuals.
incidents.impact: Credential theft targeting individuals at Taiwanese research and policy organizations; campaign leverages AI for lure generation and dynamically adapts targets to current geopolitical events.

incidents.victim: National Domain Registries — Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl), American Samoa (.as)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised domain registrar accounts controlling three national top-level domains, modifying DNS records and obtaining fraudulent TLS certificates for major sites including Google.
incidents.impact: Fraudulent TLS certificates obtained for Google and other high-value domains under three national TLDs; certificates have been revoked; scope of DNS interception and traffic manipulation during the compromise window remains under investigation.

incidents.victim: 86,644+ Organizations Globally Using Fortinet FortiGate Firewalls
incidents.vector: Scanned internet-facing FortiGate SSL VPN gateways, exploited reused and legacy SHA-256 credentials through GPU-accelerated cracking and password spraying, then sold verified device access to ransomware affiliates.
incidents.impact: Over 86,644 devices compromised across 194 countries; organizations are being locked out of their own Fortinet infrastructure; ransomware affiliates actively using purchased access for follow-on attacks.

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK Fashion Retailer)
incidents.vector: Social engineering compromised an ASOS employee account, enabling attackers to access customer records and blast unauthorized push notifications to the platform's entire customer base.
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed for an undisclosed number of users; unauthorized push notifications sent to all ASOS customers on October 6; payment cards and passwords reportedly not affected; investigation ongoing.

incidents.victim: South Korean Financial Institutions (Multiple Banks)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — AI-assisted financial theft (suspected Chinese-speaking)
incidents.vector: Used ARTEX, an open-source agentic pentesting tool developed in China and powered by LLMs (DeepSeek v4.1-flash, GLM-5.3), to conduct automated reconnaissance and exploitation of Korean bank loan inquiry and mobile work-support systems.
incidents.impact: Customer financial data exfiltrated from multiple South Korean banks in late September–early October 2026; stolen data subsequently listed for sale on Telegram by the attacker.

incidents.victim: Danish Government (National CPR Registry — 8 Million Citizens)
incidents.vector: Attackers abused a legitimate Danish company's lawful access to the national CPR civil registration system to exfiltrate citizen records without authorization.
incidents.impact: Records of 8 million Danish citizens exposed, including names, addresses, and national identification numbers; breach occurred in September 2026 and went undetected until October 2.

incidents.victim: 1,000+ Global Victims — KillSec Ransomware (Law Enforcement Action)
incidents.vector: RaaS platform offered for $250 entry fee; exploited unpatched public-facing servers using double-extortion ransomware; operated as a distributed affiliate model with a small core team.
incidents.impact: European law enforcement arrested three members in Spain, Romania, and the UK and seized infrastructure on October 2; group had executed 500+ successful attacks globally with substantial ransom receipts.

incidents.victim: Organizations Using Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway (50,000+ Exposed Instances)
incidents.vector: Exploited two critical zero-day RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772, CVSS 9.5 each) via a three-stage command injection chain to deploy PHP web shells before patches were available.
incidents.impact: Persistent remote access web shells deployed on compromised NetScaler systems since August 2026; 50,277+ potentially vulnerable instances identified globally; patches now available but compromised systems require forensic cleanup.

incidents.victim: Air Traffic and Navigation Services (ATNS), South Africa
incidents.vector: Ransomware deployed against ATNS operational technology (OT) network controlling weather and safety systems used by air traffic controllers; possible insider involvement under investigation.
incidents.impact: Air traffic weather services disrupted; attack stopped narrowly short of forcing international flight suspensions; ATNS manages 6% of the world's airspace and a full disruption would have halted flights across southern Africa.

incidents.victim: Water Utility, Telecom Provider, Regional Government, and University (Spain / Portugal)
incidents.vector: Emerging Warlock ransomware group executing a targeted campaign against large Iberian organizations across multiple sectors; specific initial access vectors under investigation.
incidents.impact: Four organizations across critical infrastructure and public sector compromised over a two-month campaign; Warlock is a newly active ransomware group with demonstrated reach into critical infrastructure in Western Europe.

incidents.victim: Arizona Court System
incidents.vector: Phishing email caused a court employee to click a malicious link, enabling unauthorized access to court backup files and the FARE financial assistance program database.
incidents.impact: 1.3 million individuals' records exposed including Social Security numbers and 30 years of case history; 150,000+ Foster Care Review Board reports accessed including data on approximately 8,000 children in foster care and protective order records.

incidents.victim: LNG Cargo Ship (Liberian-flagged, Spanish Port)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached onboard operational technology systems controlling liquefied natural gas tank pressure, safety valves, and boil-off gas management.
incidents.impact: Ship forced to make an emergency port call in Spain to prevent potential catastrophic LNG failure; one of three maritime OT security incidents reported within a single week, with FBI and US Coast Guard also boarding vessels in the Gulf of Mexico.

incidents.victim: Yoido Full Gospel Church (850,000 Members) and SaRang Church, South Korea
incidents.vector: Web shell installed via a vulnerable church application; leaked credentials and internal security flaws exploited at a second church; AI tools used for automated vulnerability analysis and lateral movement.
incidents.impact: 47+ GB of data stolen including member personal information, financial records, internal communications, and HR data for 286 employees; SAP business management systems accessed; attacker infrastructure linked to a prior US Christian media platform breach.

incidents.victim: US Department of Defense / Defense Manpower Data Center (DMDC)
incidents.vector: Vulnerability in the Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center unencrypted file-sharing platform exploited for persistent, unauthorized access over nine months without detection.
incidents.impact: Records of 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased individuals tied to the US military exposed, including Social Security numbers, names, birth dates, and military occupational data; breach ran undetected from October 2025 until July 16, 2026.

incidents.victim: iRhythm Technologies (Cardiac Biosensor / Medical Device Maker)
incidents.vector: Social engineering attack compromised an employee with access to third-party-hosted business applications containing patient health information.
incidents.impact: 360,000+ patients' protected health information stolen, including names, insurance data, device serial numbers, and clinical information; attackers subsequently issued extortion demands threatening to release patient data.

incidents.victim: npm, Go, and Rust Open-Source Package Ecosystems (Axios, Mastra AI, Rust arrayref)
incidents.vector: Compromised maintainer accounts to inject backdoors into widely-used packages; a self-propagating npm worm (ChainDrop) infected 400+ dependent packages; malware exfiltrates cloud IAM tokens and CI/CD pipeline credentials via Web3-based blockchain C2 infrastructure.
incidents.impact: 400+ npm packages infected across multiple campaigns; cloud access tokens and pipeline credentials stolen from enterprise development environments; Web3 C2 infrastructure resists takedown and the campaign remains active.

incidents.victim: Organizations Running Open-Source AI Services (LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, Gitea)
incidents.vector: Exploited misconfigured or vulnerable open-source AI infrastructure; used a poem published on GitHub to encode C2 server addresses via dictionary lookup, obscuring command-and-control traffic from detection tools.
incidents.impact: 3,400+ servers compromised for cryptomining since April 2026; malware includes remote code execution capability enabling potential abuse of hosted AI models and downstream compromise of organizations depending on these services.

incidents.victim: Iraqi Critical Infrastructure — Telecommunications and Aviation
incidents.vector: Weaponized Visual Studio coding challenge files (.csproj) delivered via spear-phishing impersonating Dubai Airports IT recruiters; AppDomainManager hijacking and DLL sideloading deployed ShelbyLoader V2 with GitHub API-based C2.
incidents.impact: Covert access established in Iraq's telecom and aviation sectors; custom ShelbyLoader V2 and Chisel tunneling utility deployed for persistent network traversal; additional targeting of Israeli and UAE entities observed in the same campaign.
